title: Online play that feels local: a menu before connecting, yourself moved locally, rules on raw state, a loopback demo, in Rust
note: Online play is sim.net: connect only after Play online, move yourself locally, draw remotes from state(), rule on state_raw(), host-only shared keys.
intent: Multiplayer is sim.net, read like input. Register game.net(NetConfig::new().publish_hz(15).decimals(2).interp_delay_ticks(6)) once and set [net] enabled = true in genex.toml; without it every build is offline (net-disabled), so the game must still play locally. Never connect on boot: sim.net.connect() or sim.net.matchmake() only after the player picks Play online, and sim.net.leave() when they go back. Move yourself on the input tick and publish with sim.net.set_me(json!(..)) (coalesced; snap_me for a respawn); never wait for your echo. Draw sim.net.remotes() from state() (smoothed, drawing only); every gameplay rule (hits, scores) reads .state_raw(). Teams, rounds and scores are sim.net.set_shared keys only the host writes (sim.net.is_host()); write an object only after an accepted sim.net.claim. Read sim.net.events() every tick and pause a round while sim.net.connected() is below its minimum. A refused write answers a NetError whose code() is typed (net-not-joined, net-not-host). Prove it with a demo: driver.net() joins scripted players in Studio's loopback room. Online play is proved only on the published draft in two windows; until then say multiplayer was not exercised.
port: One facet owns game.net, the menu's commitment point and the room's events; other facets read sim.net and write only their own objects.

evidence.note: sim.net reads and writes, the loopback room in Studio, scripted players through driver.net(), the refusals and the feel rules.
Menu before online, render yourself locally, test raw, host-only shared state, claim before host simulation, quorum.
